newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power up slightly, but loads down.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power up slightly, but loads down.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the western U.S. moved slightly higher Wednesday amid scattered power plant outages, but cooler weather kept the market from posting bigger gains, trade sources said.
"The market has loosened up a bit with the change in weather," said a California trader.
California-Oregon border prices for Wednesday were last quoted $17.50-18.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), up slightly from $17.00-18.00 on Tuesday.
Wednesday Palo Verde prices were quoted $20.00-21.00, little changed from $20.00-22.00 on Tuesday.
Edison Intl's Southern California Edison Co said one of the two 790 MW units at its Mohave coal-fired power plant in Nevada tripped off-line early Wednesday and will likely be down until Monday.
On Tuesday, Edison's 1,080 MW San Onofre nuclear unit 3 was shut for unplanned work on the reactor's coolant system. It is expected to be out of service for about two weeks.
Also, PacifiCorp said one of the four 550 MW units at its Jim Bridger coal-fired plant in Wyoming should be back up Thursday, after begin shut Saturday for repairs to a fan.
But traders said cooler weather, especially in the desert Southwest, was putting a damper on spot market prices.
"The outages are kind of countering the weather," said another trader. "There is not too much load build-up during the day."
October COB prices were last quoted $16.10-16.20 per MWh, compared with $16.00-16.25 per Mwh on Tuesday. Palo Verde for October was quoted $16.40-16.60, up from $16.25-16.40 on Tuesday.
